newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mulling wheat flour, malt export subsidies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mulling wheat flour, malt export subsidies.

text.p: A sharp drop in wheat flour and barley malt exports over the past several years could spur U.S. Agriculture Department to resume export subsidies for those commodities, a department aide said Monday.
But any decision to take that action could still be some time away because of the $10 million cap on Export Enhancement Program spending in fiscal 1997,the aide said.
Wheat flour and barley malt are "two areas of concern given the drop in our global market share" over the past several years, the aide said.
According to USDA statistics, U.S. wheat flour exports in 1996/97 (June-May) totaled just 162,500 tonnes, down from 240,100 the previous year and 568,300 in 1994-95.
USDA does not publish barley malt export data. But an industry source said exports in 1996/97 were neglible compared to 66,400 tonnes in 1995/96 and nearly 75,000 in 1995-96.
Last week, USDA announced allocations for countries to buy wheat flour, barley malt and a number of other commodities under EEP in 1997-98 (July-June).
But USDA has not actually "activated" any of those allocations yet. Until that happens, "they're meaningless," an industry aide noted.
